proof.text:
The universal property gives a canonical isomorphism \(Y_U\cong U\times_B T_B\), so the square for \((f_U,g_B)\) is Cartesian and \(ce_U=ed\). For the representative calculation below there is a canonical map
\[
 \kappa:Y_U\times_{T_B}(T_B\times_BW)\longrightarrow
 Y\times_T(T\times_SW)
\]
induced by \(d:Y_U\to Y\), \(c:T_B\to T\), and \(\mathrm{id}_W\). This map is not asserted to be an isomorphism. For an object \(Q\to U\) of \(U_{\mathrm{Et}}\) and \(W\to B\) etale with a map \(Q\to W\) over \(B\), identify \(Y_U\times_UQ\) with \(Y\times_XQ\) (\(Q\) over \(X\) through \(a\)) by the canonical isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product], and let \(\ell_{\mathrm{glob}}=(\mathrm{pr}_Y,(e\,\mathrm{pr}_Y,Q\to W)):Y\times_XQ\to Y\times_T(T\times_SW)\) and \(\ell_{\mathrm{loc}}=(\mathrm{pr}_{Y_U},(e_U\mathrm{pr}_{Y_U},Q\to W)):Y_U\times_UQ\to Y_U\times_{T_B}(T_B\times_BW)\). Then \(\kappa\circ\ell_{\mathrm{loc}}=(d\,\mathrm{pr}_{Y_U},(c\,e_U\mathrm{pr}_{Y_U},Q\to W))=(\mathrm{pr}_Y,(e\,d\,\mathrm{pr}_{Y_U},Q\to W))=\ell_{\mathrm{glob}}\), using \(ce_U=ed\) and the uniqueness in the universal property of the fibre product. The commutativity \(fa=bf_U\) gives the required square maps, and the inverse-image composition comparisons are the canonical ones.

proof.text: Apply the slice-site localization comparison to \(g:T\to S\) at \(B\to S\) and to \(h:Y\to X\) at \(U\to X\). It gives the natural direct-image and inverse-image comparisons on the two slices, while the open-etale localization lemma identifies those slices with \(B_{\mathrm{Et}},U_{\mathrm{Et}}\). The set and abelian inverse-image/restriction lemmas then give the displayed natural maps \(C_L\) and \(C_R\), for both coefficient categories. At this stage these are only the canonical localization comparisons; no mate equality is being assumed.

proof.text: We record how \(C_L\) acts on a representative. A local representative of a section of \(f_U^{-1}g_{B*}F_B\) over \(Q\to U\) is \((W\to B,\ a:Q\to U\times_BW\text{ over }U,\ s_B)\) with \(s_B\in F_B(T_B\times_BW)\); since \(T_B\times_BW\cong T\times_SW\) canonically [def-pc-fibre-product] and \(F_B=r_{T_B}F\), \(s_B\) is the image of a unique \(s\in F(T\times_SW)=(g_*F)(W\to S)\) under restriction along that isomorphism. Viewing \(W\) over \(S\) through \(b\), the global representative is \((W\to S,\ a':Q\to X\times_SW,\ s)\), where \(a'\) has \(X\)-component \(Q\to U\xrightarrow{a}X\) and \(W\)-component that of \(a\). \(C_L\) carries the class of \((W\to S,a',s)\) in \((r_Uf^{-1}g_*F)(Q)\) to the class of \((W\to B,a,s_B)\): the first component of \(C_L\), \(r_Uf^{-1}\cong a^{-1}f^{-1}\cong(fa)^{-1}=(bf_U)^{-1}\cong f_U^{-1}b^{-1}\cong f_U^{-1}r_B\), sends \(a'^*(f^*s)\) to \(a^*(f_U^*s)\) by the unit formula \(c_{f,g,F}(g^*(f^*s))=(f\circ g)^*s\) applied to both factorizations, together with the restriction formula \(\rho(j^*s)=s|\) for the etale inverse images along \(a\) and \(b\) and naturality of these sheaf maps along \(Q\to(X\times_SW)\times_XU\) and \(W\to W\times_SB\); the second component of \(C_L\) is, sectionwise at \(W\to B\), restriction along \(T_B\times_BW\cong T\times_SW\), sending \(s\) to \(s_B\). The same calculation applies to abelian sections, using the abelian composition and restriction isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Let \(Q\to U\) be an object and \((W\to B,a,s_B)\) a local representative as in step 3, with global representative \((W\to S,a',s)\). Apply the set-valued sectionwise exchange node (for sheaves of sets) or the abelian one (for abelian sheaves) to the global square \((f,g,h,e)\), Cartesian by [sbc-def-base-change-square], at the object \(Q\to X\): \(r_U(\beta_F)\) sends the class of \((W,a',s)\) to \(\ell_{\mathrm{glob}}^*(e^*s)\in(e^{-1}F)(Y\times_XQ)\). Apply the same node to the local square \((f_U,g_B,h_U,e_U)\), Cartesian by step 1: \(\beta_{U,F_B}\) sends the class of \((W,a,s_B)\) to \(\ell_{\mathrm{loc}}^*(e_U^*s_B)\in(e_U^{-1}F_B)(Y_U\times_UQ)\). Now compute \(C_R\). Its first component is, at \(Q\), restriction along \(Y_U\times_UQ\cong Y\times_XQ\) (the direct images are evaluation on base-changed objects [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]). Its second component \(r_{Y_U}e^{-1}F\cong d^{-1}e^{-1}F\cong(ed)^{-1}F=(ce_U)^{-1}F\cong e_U^{-1}c^{-1}F\cong e_U^{-1}F_B\) sends \(\kappa^*(e^*s)\) (a section over the object \(Y_U\times_{T_B}(T_B\times_BW)\) of \(Y_{U,\mathrm{Et}}\)) to \(e_U^*s_B\): the restriction formulas for \(d\) and \(c\) and the unit formula of the composition isomorphisms for both factorizations of \(ed=ce_U\) identify both with the unit image of \(s\) for the composite, and \(c^*s\) corresponds to \(s_B\). Since \(C_R\) is a morphism of sheaves it commutes with restriction along the \(Y_U\)-morphism \(\ell_{\mathrm{loc}}\), and step 1 gives \(\kappa\ell_{\mathrm{loc}}=\ell_{\mathrm{glob}}\). Hence
\[
 C_R\bigl(\ell_{\mathrm{glob}}^*(e^*s)\bigr)=\ell_{\mathrm{loc}}^*\bigl(C_R(\kappa^*e^*s)\bigr)=\ell_{\mathrm{loc}}^*(e_U^*s_B),
\]
that is, \(C_R\circ r_U(\beta_F)\circ C_L^{-1}\) and \(\beta_{U,F_B}\) agree on the class of every local presheaf representative over every \(Q\to U\). The abelian case is the same computation with the abelian composition and restriction isomorphisms.

proof.text: The sheaf \(f_U^{-1}g_{B*}F_B\) is the sheafification of the presheaf of local representatives [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Two morphisms of sheaves out of a sheafification that agree after composing with the canonical map from the presheaf are equal, by the uniqueness in the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Step 4 shows this agreement for \(C_R\circ r_U(\beta_F)\circ C_L^{-1}\) and \(\beta_{U,F_B}\), so they are equal; composing with the isomorphism \(C_L\) gives \(C_R\circ r_U(\beta_F)=\beta_{U,F_B}\circ C_L\). Both sides are composites of natural transformations in \(F\) (\(\beta\), \(C_L\), \(C_R\) and \(F\mapsto F_B\) are natural), so the identity is natural in \(F\).

title: Underived base-change arrow under etale localization
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:T\to S$ be morphisms of schemes, with the Cartesian square $Y=X\times_ST$, $h:Y\to X$, $e:Y\to T$ [sbc-def-base-change-square]. Let $a:U\to X$ and $b:B\to S$ be etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $f_U:U\to B$ satisfy $fa=bf_U$. Put $T_B=B\times_ST$, with projections $g_B:T_B\to B$ and $c:T_B\to T$, and $Y_U=U\times_XY$, with projections $h_U:Y_U\to U$ and $d:Y_U\to Y$. The canonical identification $Y_U\cong U\times_BT_B$ defines $e_U:Y_U\to T_B$, so $ce_U=ed$. Work on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], and write $r_Z$ for restriction to an etale object $Z$. For a sheaf $F$ of sets or abelian groups on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], put $F_B=r_{T_B}F$. Use the inverse/direct-image adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] and [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], with direct images as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Define $\beta_F:f^{-1}g_*F\to h_*e^{-1}F$ as the transpose under $h^{-1}\dashv h_*$ of
$$h^{-1}f^{-1}g_*F\xrightarrow{\theta_\square}e^{-1}g^{-1}g_*F\xrightarrow{e^{-1}\varepsilon_g}e^{-1}F,$$
where $\theta_\square$ is the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphism; define $\beta_{U,F_B}$ by the same formula for $(f_U,g_B,h_U,e_U)$. The canonical comparisons
$$C_L:r_Uf^{-1}g_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}f_U^{-1}r_Bg_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}f_U^{-1}g_{B*}F_B,$$
$$C_R:r_Uh_*e^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{U*}r_{Y_U}e^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{U*}e_U^{-1}F_B,$$
formed from inverse-image composition, etale inverse-image/restriction, and direct-image slice localization [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition], [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction], [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], [lem-weil-pbc-slice-site-localization], satisfy
$$C_R\circ r_U(\beta_F)=\beta_{U,F_B}\circ C_L.$$
The identity is natural in $F$.
